items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: Thank goodness that Mongo Santamaria in 1987 gave me the opportunity to join his band

ctx.x: You’re not going to be talking either.

No. You’ve got to go in there and get — so I was doing that, I was doing contemporary classical music — like I traveled around the world with — one of the last projects I did was with Osvaldo Golijov. He’s a conductor of contemporary classical music from Argentina. He’s a composer rather, of contemporary classical music from Argentina. We traveled all over the world. And I wasn’t playing bebop on that. I was playing C trumpet, piccolo trumpet and B flat trumpet in this work that he had. Right? Again was I playing…

sunrise service and you’ve got to go in there and play “The Trumpet Shall Sound” and Handel’s “Messiah” on D trumpet. Okay, get ready, and you’re going to go there with your puffy salsa chops going in there. And was I doing it because I necessarily wanted it? I was proud of my skill set and I would do it, but my endorphins were not going woo this is awesome. This is about I have to pay my bills. You know? So I often tell my students when I first started to break in like the salsa music scene man I was not the…
